# v0.24.7 — long-running sessions keep their summary, no compaction wait below the threshold, no level 3 fragments, a bounded summary prefix, steer rows stored, and the plugin stays enabled on Hermes with the plugin package manager (#650, #651, #652, #653, #633, #612, #631, #677, #678)

Qualified at the release candidate tag `v0.24.7-rc2` (`c60fed3a`): this GA tree is that tree plus this file
(RELEASE-READINESS-V1; `git diff --name-status v0.24.7-rc2..v0.24.7` = only this file).
`v0.24.7-rc1` (`9bbfb8f1`) is superseded: on Hermes with the plugin package manager it is disabled at the next update
(#631), and it carried two defects this release fixes (#677, #678; see "Changes").

Patch release on top of `v0.24.6` (`ae0e996d`). Runtime change: what the survival fit keeps, what an automatic
compaction does below the threshold or after a pass that made no progress, when a level 3 summary may be written,
which summary nodes the prefix keeps, which unstamped rows the identity audit checks, and which formatting mistakes
the summary contract tolerates.
- No tool name or count, commit-proof wire format (version 3), store schema or privacy posture changed; `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name
  are unchanged. The `lcm_status` output grows additively: a `no_progress_hold` field and three sweep fields (`pre_leaf_condensation_passes`,
  `pre_leaf_condensation_stop_reason`, `post_drain_condensation_skipped`), and a condensation can report the
  suppression reason `summary_result_rejected`.
- Three new environment switches, from #614: `LCM_LEAF_TARGET_RATIO`, `LCM_LEAF_TARGET_MIN_TOKENS` and
  `LCM_LEAF_TARGET_MAX_TOKENS`. With the defaults every leaf target is unchanged. No other key was added.
- No change below deletes or rewrites a stored row; the raw rows behind every summary stay reachable by the `lcm_*` tools.
- This release never moves a deployed pin by itself. A deployment moves only when its operator re-pins it.

## Changes since v0.24.6 (every change issue-first, reviewed at its exact head, receipted on its PR)

- **#650 (#654): the survival fit keeps LCM's summary.**
  - **Before.** On Hermes the summary prefix is the oldest row of the list, and the fit always cut from the oldest row,
    so every fit removed the summary block with the oldest raw rows and, with no system row, gave no notice either. On
    deployed profiles there were 31 fits on 5 profiles, 13 of them in the last 12 hours; each left the model without
    its summary until the next compaction.
  - **The fit.** It now keeps the generated summary prefix and removes only whole oldest turns after it, choosing the
    cut by the final list's size, notice included. The notice is written only into a real system row.
  - **A carrier.** When Hermes has merged the summary into the first user row, the fit splits that row, lets the user
    row leave with its reply, and re-forms the merged row as assembly would.
  - **The fallback.** When no whole-turn cut can hold the prefix, the previous rule applies, with a WARNING
    `LCM survival fit dropped the summary prefix (emergency: …)`. The result is never larger than v0.24.6's.
- **#651 (#655): no summariser pass below the threshold, and a stop after a pass that made no progress.**
  - **Before.** On the busiest deployed profiles, users waited about 1.7 hours a day inside their own turns for
    compactions (28% of interactive turn time); 37% of that wait was the plugin's own below-threshold maintenance
    running a full leaf pass. Nothing stopped a pass that made no progress, and the host's anti-thrash breaker could
    not trip for this plugin.
  - **Below the threshold.** An automatic compress() only cleans up (ingest, sanitation, cursor alignment); no summariser.
  - **The hold.** A threshold pass that stored no leaf and did not shrink the list starts a finite hold (the #608
    constant, 600 s). A host refusal starts it too, through `record_rejected_compaction`. A stored leaf or the time ends
    it. While it holds, automatic threshold compaction is off.
  - **Never blocked by the hold:** manual `/compress`, forced overflow, a host recovery attempt, the survival ceiling
    and sessions that bypass LCM.
  - **The host gate.** Hosts with the breaker gate (`_automatic_compression_blocked`) read the hold as a transient
    `cooldown:lcm_*` block.
- **#652 (#666): no level 3 fragments while the survival fit can rescue the request.**
  - **Before.** A leaf whose summary results were rejected at levels 1 and 2 was written as a level 3 truncation. On
    `v0.24.6`, a route that always fails produced about 3 such leaves in an engine's first compaction and then 1 per
    cooldown. The real-host cells below show 3 per cell (empty output) and 1 (errors).
  - **Now.** On a non-forced compaction with a working survival fit, a level 3 that actually truncated is rejected:
    - a leaf stops the sweep, and its rows stay for a later compaction;
    - a condensation leaves its nodes on the frontier.

    A level 3 that is its whole source loses nothing and is still written. Forced overflow, fit off and an unknown
    window converge through level 3 as before.
  - **The sweep deadline.** In a threshold sweep, every summariser attempt (each route, each level) gets at most the
    time left before the sweep's 120 s deadline. An attempt that would start with less than 15 s left is not started,
    and running out of time never produces a level 3 node; the rows stay for a later compaction.
- **#653 (#666): a bounded summary prefix that keeps the newest nodes.**
  - **Before.** A threshold sweep that ran out of budget never reached its condensation, so the summary prefix grew
    with every compaction.
  - **Condense first.** When the prefix is already over its target, it is now condensed first, in at most half the
    sweep's passes and time.
  - **Newest-first assembly.** When the prefix exceeds its budget, the newest parts of each depth are kept. Only the
    nodes actually placed in the prefix count as visible for recall dedupe.
- **#633 (#657): a mid-turn `/steer` is stored.**
  - **Before.** Hermes 0.21.2 and later insert the steer as an unstamped user row before the plugin's ingest cursor,
    and the identity audit only checked stamped rows, so the user's instruction was never stored.
  - **Now.** The audit also checks unstamped user rows the host inserted, each against its own stored copy; a repeated
    identical steer is stored again. The insertion diff is capped at 1,000,000 row comparisons (about 40 ms); above the
    cap the v0.24.6 behaviour applies. The in-place shape of Hermes 0.21.1 and earlier, and `LCM_IDENTITY_ANCHOR=0`, are
    not covered.
- **#612 (#656): the summary contract tolerates three named formatting mistakes.**
  - **Before.** In the field, one model tier broke the contract on 7 of 7 summary calls; the other tiers broke it on
    none of about 203.
  - **The three mistakes:** a `</summary>` closer, one `<summary>` wrapper around the whole body, and one layer of quotes
    or emphasis on the closing hint.
  - **Still required:** the exact nonce opening tag, its uniqueness, the body minimum and a recognised closing hint.
  - **The discard WARNING** keeps `violated the integrity contract` and adds `check=<envelope|nonce_count|short_body|
    closing_hint>`.
- **#614 (#647): leaf-target settings** (the three keys above). The defaults leave every target unchanged.
- **rc2 — #631 (#676): the plugin stays enabled on Hermes with the plugin package manager.**
  - **Before.** Hermes after `v2026.9.24` has a plugin package manager that treats a plugin checkout with any
    `pyproject.toml` as a uv workspace member. Ours held lint settings only, so the project entry had no version,
    `uv lock` failed, and the update put `hermes-lcm-x` under `plugins.disabled`: the profile ran without LCM
    (`Context engine 'lcm-x' not found`), and a plain `plugins enable` was refused by the same check. Every release
    through `v0.24.7-rc1` is affected on such a Hermes; stable tags through `v2026.9.24` have no package manager.
  - **Now.** The lint settings live in `ruff.toml`; there is no `pyproject.toml` and no `uv.lock`, so the checkout is
    not a member. No runtime file changed. Thanks to #632, which found the same failure.
- **rc2 — #677 (#679): the host's count decides below the threshold.**
  - **Before.** #651 made below-threshold maintenance cleanup-only only when LCM-X's own count was also below the
    threshold. When the host counted under it and LCM-X at or over it, a summariser pass still ran (in the field, 1 of
    21 below-threshold maintenance events, about 5% of that wait); so did a direct `compress()` right after a refused
    compaction.
  - **Now.** An automatic compaction that follows the engine's own preflight request is cleanup-only when the host's
    count is below the threshold, and so is an automatic compaction the no-progress hold blocks (the hold never blocks
    the survival ceiling). It does not change forced compaction, overflow recovery or `/compress` (#684 is older).
- **rc2 — #678 (#679): the survival fit protects only a verified summary.**
  - **Before.** In rc1 the fit took any row with an LCM summary header as the prefix, even a user row quoting one for a
    node that does not exist, and then cut the reply after it alone. `v0.24.6` was not affected.
  - **Now.** The prefix must match a stored summary node of this session byte for byte. A row that does not verify is
    an ordinary row, as in `v0.24.6`.

## Known follow-ups

- #644: a drop-only survival fit, or a cold re-ingest of a list missing stored tail rows, can re-store rows (duplicates only).
- v0.24.8 (repairs): a doctor repair for existing level 3 nodes and the condensed nodes built from them (#667), no
  level 3 cut in rollups (#669), forced-recovery stubs (#636), a recovery call after a boundary-cooldown preflight that
  is still cleanup-only (#684), and a store open at load that can wait behind the daily integrity check (#622).
- v0.24.9 (drain): a wall-clock budget on the whole foreground compaction, larger hidden-row leaves with a capped
  output (#597), an exit fit below the host threshold (#668), and an off-turn drain of hidden rows (#610, #626).
- A steer in the in-place shape of Hermes 0.21.1 and earlier is still not stored (#633 scope).
- #665: a refused compaction in a session that bypasses LCM can start the foreground session's no-progress hold.
- #681: a user row that is a byte-exact copy of a same-session summary still counts as that summary in the fit, and a
  user row that starts with Hermes' task-list banner counts as that host row: the fit can then cut its reply alone.
- #682: a summary route that pairs a model with a provider that does not serve it fails every summary call; set
  `auxiliary.compression.provider` and `auxiliary.compression.model` together in the profile's `config.yaml`.
- Correction (#685): the operator guide and the skill reference still describe a stored level 3 leaf to open with
  `lcm_expand`; since #652 a normal compaction writes no such leaf and keeps its rows for the next pass.

## Benchmark boundary

- No retrieval or QA benchmark claim is made by this release; the qualification is lifecycle reliability on real hosts.

## Upgrade

- Plugin only: verify the exact commit, install this tag at it and restart the gateway. The store needs no migration,
  and a rollback to `v0.24.6` is plugin-only.
- **A profile the package manager already disabled** (`Context engine 'lcm-x' not found` in its log; `hermes-lcm-x` under
  `plugins.disabled`): a plain `plugins enable` is refused. Install this tag's commit with the enable flag, then restart
  the gateway:
  `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 hermes --profile <profile> plugins install https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x --force --ref <commit> --enable`.
  The install exits 0 even when admission refuses: confirm that `hermes-lcm-x` is no longer under `plugins.disabled`
  in the profile's `config.yaml` and that the log shows `registered context engine: lcm-x`. The variable keeps that one
  command from running Hermes' dependency sync and interface rebuilds.
